summary:
Factors are at least 1, so extending a run never lowers its product: a counting window works. Multiply in each
factor; while the product is at least `cap`, divide out the leftmost factor. Then all `r − left + 1` runs ending
at `r` are under the cap. A cap of 0 or 1 admits nothing. O(n).

question.md:
Count the contiguous runs of `factors` whose product is strictly less than `cap`.

- **n up to 10⁵**, factors 1..1000, cap up to 10⁶.

think.md:
`factors = [3, 2, 5, 1, 4, 6, 1]`, `cap = 25` → **18**.

Products of positive integers grow (or stay the same, with 1s) as a run is extended, so the runs ending at `r`
that are under the cap are exactly those starting at or after some `left`. The window keeps the product below
`cap` (at most 10⁶), so multiplying in one more factor stays below 10⁹: no overflow, and division by the
leaving factor is exact.

idea.md: For each start, multiply while the product stays under the cap, counting each run.

lines.text: Multiply in the next factor; once at or above the cap, longer runs are too (64-bit: one factor past 10⁶ stays below 10⁹).

complexity.md: **Time O(n²)** when many factors are 1. **Space O(1).**

walk.title: From each start, multiply as you extend; stop once the product reaches the cap.

limits.md: Long runs of 1s make every start extend far. The window keeps one product for all starts.

approaches.title: Counting window with a running product

idea.md: If `cap ≤ 1`, return 0. Otherwise multiply in `factors[r]`; while `product ≥ cap`, divide by `factors[left]` and advance. Add `r − left + 1`.

lines.text: Every product is at least 1, so a cap of 0 or 1 admits no run (this also keeps the shrink loop from running past `i`).
Divide out factors from the left until the product is under the cap; division is exact since they were multiplied in.
Every start from `left` to `i` gives a run under the cap.

walk.title: Keep the product of the window. Multiply in each new factor; while the product is at least the cap, divide out factors from the left. Every start in the window gives a run ending here.

takeaways.md:
- **Products of factors ≥ 1** behave like sums of non-negatives: windows work.
- Handle `cap ≤ 1` first, or the window would try to shrink past empty.
- Counting windows add `r − left + 1` per end.
